text:
eli: FYI I have a repro that shows steady KV cache memory growth on our on-prem GPU nodes after the "rescan" heuristic landed. Appears only on private clusters with the 6.1+ kernel.
neha: Can you paste the short steps to repro? 
eli: minimal repro: (1) start long-chat workload with 8k contexts, (2) enable rescan heuristic (default in 2026-02), (3) issue streams of 1k concurrent inference threads with --max-new-tokens 2048. After ~3h the KV size climbs and we see elevated page_faults.
juan: Does this happen on Dedicated or Hosted?
eli: Not on hosted — hosted shows stable KV reuse. Dedicated sometimes shows small bumps but stabilizes after GC. Private (onprem) steadily grows until OOM or paging.
sasha: I captured /proc/pid/smaps + perf counters. Key bits: 
```
KV_cache_alloc: 19.4G -> 26.1G over 3h
major_faults: +12k
anon_huge_pages: stable
rss: climbs in step with kv_alloc
numa_migrate: small
```
Looks like pages are being remapped rather than freed; fragmentation increases.
perf-bot: [alert] perf-regression: kv-rescan-heuristic increased page-faults 2.3x on linux-6.1 kernels on our benchmark nodes. See /artifacts/1738456789/perf.json
samir: Possible vectors: (a) kernel's page reclaim interacts badly with our jemalloc arenas and hugepage alignment, (b) rescan heuristic causes more small allocations that defeat the slab coalescer on older drivers, (c) networked storage in VPC (Private) delays reclaim ack -> observed dirty page backlog.
neha: I can run a bisect on the heuristic config. Can you push the exact env/settings?
eli: repro env: REDWOOD_KV_RESCAN=1 (default), REDWOOD_KV_RECLAIM_THRESHOLD=0.6, kernel=6.1.8-custom, glibc=2.35, jemalloc=5.2.1. Command I used: 
```
./run_infer --model gpt-4-ish --workload longcontext --concurrency 1000 --max-new-tokens 2048
```
I also toggled REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=0 and saw marginal improvement.
juan: Is kernel selection different across fleets? I recall Dedicated nodes pinned to a distro with custom patches; Hosted uses our managed images and private onprem is whatever customer has. If the kernel picks a different page frame eviction path (shmem vs anon) maybe behavior diverges.
sasha: I ran a small perf trace (stack fragment):
```
kmem_cache_alloc -> __jemalloc_arena_malloc -> kv_alloc -> do_page_cache_reclaim -> handle_mm_fault
```
We get many handle_mm_fault hits on the onprem run.
neha: Could the rescan heuristic be keeping KV pages mapped but orphaning them from our reclaim lists? That would look like increased RSS but not returned to OS.
eli: Exactly. On private nodes, the vmlinux config seems to cause deferred KSM-like scannings. Also saw odd skbuff/rdma interactions when the node has Mellanox driver 5.x loaded.
samir: Short mitigation options: 
- roll back rescan heuristic (set REDWOOD_KV_RESCAN=0) on onprem images for now.
- increase REDWOOD_KV_RECLAIM_THRESHOLD to 0.8 to trigger earlier eviction.
- force jemalloc background purge: set MALLOC_CONF="background_thread:true,dirty_decay_ms:1000,muzzy_decay_ms:1000"
- pin model shards to fewer NUMA nodes and reduce extraneous allocations during warmup.

eli: I tested disabling rescan in a small private cluster: growth stops, page_faults drop to baseline. Good short-term.
juan: For Dedicated: we should add a validation job that runs long-context traces under the distro/kernel matrix we support. If a kernel variant regresses we auto-fail the rollout.
neha: I'll open a bug and add the bisect steps. We should include perf snapshots for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and highlight kernel config bits: CONFIG_HUGETLB_PAGE, THP, vm.swappiness, and network drivers loaded.
sasha: Also capture pmap and migrate counters and /proc/slabinfo at 30m intervals. That helped me correlate fragmentation spikes with jemalloc arena growth.
perf-bot: [note] queued benchmark: kv-cache-longrun-matrix (kernels: 5.15, 6.1, 6.4) assigned to eng-runtime/perf for next run.
eli: Plan: (1) push rollback for rescan to onprem CI images and notify customers on Private rollout; (2) add dedicated matrix job; (3) follow-up with kernel devs if we can isolate specific config flags; (4) track remediation in bug #RLW-1428 (I created it).
samir: I'll take the kernel-onprem investigation. neha + sasha will own the repro/metrics pack. eli please paste any extra logs into RLW-1428.
eli: done. thanks all. :thumbsup:
